narrative:
The model determined that you have a 65% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the purpose of the loan, and the level of your savings. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This situation pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your request for a furniture or equipment loan worked modestly in your favor. This purpose is fairly common among approved loans (21% of approvals), and the model viewed it as slightly less risky than some other uses. Similarly, your credit amount of 1,131 DM is much lower than the average of about 3,020 DM for approved applicants, which also helped your case somewhat.

Unfortunately, these positive elements were not enough to overcome the negative signal from your checking-account status and low savings (<100 DM). The combination led the model to conclude you are more likely to struggle with repayment.

You should focus on building a positive checking-account balance and increasing your savings over the next few months. Once those improve, reapply. This is the most direct way to change how a similar model would evaluate your application in the future. (218 words)
